page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-64 is a compute instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. Built on the 64-bit Arm architecture (arm64), this configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed base frequency of 3.6 GHz. Because each core hosts a single hardware execution thread without simultaneous multithreading, workloads receive predictable single-threaded execution performance across all 32 dedicated vCPUs.

The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It operates without dedicated hardware accelerators or local NVMe storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be addressed through network-attached block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the instance at launch.

Given the density of dedicated AmpereOne-M cores and the 2 GB per core memory profile, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-64 exhibits strong cost efficiency for scale-out parallel processing. The lack of SMT thread contention makes it well-suited for compute-focused tasks, containerized application runtimes, continuous integration build clusters, and parallel web service architectures designed for native Arm64 execution.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-64 is an Arm-based cloud instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 3.6 GHz on the arm64 architecture, operating with one thread per core for 32 total vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 core-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistent data. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided. With dedicated single-threaded cores and an efficient memory profile, the instance delivers consistent compute density for scale-out parallel architectures, software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, container hosting, and distributed web serving workloads.
